events.title: The death of St. James of the Marches
events.shortBlurb: The tireless Observant friar who preached the Holy Name across half of Europe and founded charitable lending houses for the poor died at Naples…
body: Born about 1391 at Monteprandone in the March of Ancona, of a poor family named Gangala, he studied law at Perugia, entered the Friars Minor, and formed himself under St. Bernardine of Siena, embracing an austerity so severe that his master had to bid him moderate his fasts. He was ordained about 1420.

With St. John of Capistrano he became one of the great preachers of the Observant reform, journeying on foot through Italy, Germany, Bohemia, Poland, Hungary, and Bosnia. He spread the devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus under the monogram IHS, served as inquisitor and papal legate against heresy, reconciled feuding cities, and promoted the Monti di Pietà — charitable pawnshops that lent to the poor at little or no interest to spare them the usurer.

Sent by the pope in his last years to Naples, he died there on 28 November 1476 and was buried in the Franciscan church of Santa Maria la Nova, his body venerated as incorrupt. Beatified by Urban VIII in 1624 and canonized by Benedict XIII in 1726, he is honored among the patrons of Naples.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “St. James of the Marches”
